ios.desc:
Paste remembers everything you copy — text, links, images, files — on Mac, iPhone, and iPad. So the thing you copied yesterday, last week, or last month is always one shortcut away.

Trusted for 10 years by designers, developers, writers, lawyers, and support teams. Recognized by Apple as an "invaluable utility."

NEVER LOSE A COPY AGAIN
Your clipboard normally holds one item. Paste holds them all.
– Unlimited clipboard history across all your devices
– Clear visual previews — see exactly what you copied, and where it came from
– Rules that automatically skip passwords and other sensitive content

FIND ANYTHING IN SECONDS
– Search everything you've ever copied — even text inside screenshots and photos
– Filter by app, date, device, or content type
– Jump straight from a search result to its place in your history

PASTE AT THE SPEED OF THOUGHT
– Open Paste in any app with a single shortcut
– Paste recent items instantly with ⌘1–9
– Queue items in Paste Stack and paste them in order — perfect for forms and repetitive work
– Paste as plain text whenever you want formatting gone

EVERYWHERE YOU WORK
– iCloud sync keeps Mac, iPhone, and iPad perfectly in step
– Hand off items between devices mid-task
– On iOS: the Paste Keyboard brings your whole history into any app
– Works seamlessly alongside Universal Clipboard

ORGANIZE AND COLLABORATE
– Keep the important stuff on Pinboards — snippets, templates, and assets that never expire
– Share Pinboards with your team, family, or clients
– You decide who can view and who can edit

WORKS WITH YOUR AI TOOLS
– Connect your clipboard history to Claude, Cursor, and other AI assistants with built-in MCP support (Mac)
– Polish copied text with Apple Intelligence Writing Tools

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
– Your data lives on your devices and in your private iCloud — never on our servers
– Hide Paste from screen sharing and recordings
– Pause capture any time

Try Paste free for one week. Subscriptions (monthly or annual), a Family plan, and a one-time Lifetime purchase unlock everything on Mac, iPhone, and iPad.

"I don't know how I lived without it" — the thing users tell us most. Copy something. You'll see.

Learn more: pasteapp.io
Say hello: pasteapp.io/contact or @paste_app on X

quotes.text:
I wonder if it's this one: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/paste-clipboard-manager/id967805235

I've noticed that more and more apps on both macOS and iOS sniff the clipboard contents and randomly clobber it. I usually notice it in apps like Sourcetree, where I'll click something or do a certain action and suddenly I can't paste anymore. I even get a feel for it, like my mind detects the pattern that empties the clipboard so I sense when I can no longer paste, but I can't figure out concrete repeatable steps to make it happen. On iOS it's more random, and I feel like it's probably Facebook doing it, or maybe websites in Safari. I just assume that everything is spying on my clipboard contents now, hoping to log secrets/passwords and PII to sell to scammers.

I have to say, this is one of the more disappointing developments from Apple, that they certainly must know by now about these clipboard shenanigans, but have done nothing to stop them. They need to implement permissions that deny all apps the ability to get/set the clipboard by default, and have an option to ask the user whether so-and-so app can access the clipboard (outside of normal copy/paste), every time with the option to allow always. And all clipboard access attempts should probably get logged somewhere.
